messages.subject: error in unite()
messages.body_plain:
Dear Reader,

I am trying to follow the steps on the methylKit page on Googlle Code.

I have read in my samples using the read.bismark function and now try to unite the methylation calls.

However, I just get the following error:

> meth = unite(myobj, destrand=TRUE)
Error in setkeyv(copy(y), by) :
  4 arguments passed to .Internal(nchar) which requires 3

and am thus kind of stuck…

I trace the error back to the ‘ data.table’  function used in ‘ .CpG.dinuc.unify’
( .CpG.dinuc.unifyOld  does work, but then later on data.table is used more often…)

Any help is appreciated!

Regards,
Aldo Jongejan

AMC Disclaimer : http://www.amc.nl/disclaimer

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] combining and analysing different samples vs control
messages.body_plain:
In your last case, you can treat 2ug & 8ug as test and 0ug as control. you need to change the treatment vector when reading all the samples or if you have all the samples in a methylBase object, you can alter the treatment vector using reorganize() function.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Calculation method for region methylation
messages.body_plain:
Dear authors,

The calculation method for region methylation in methylkit is
the sum of methylated cytosine reads / the sum of reads covered on the all cytosines in the region.

But we found most publications use another method to calculate the region methylation:
the average methylation level for all cytosines in the region.

My question is what is the advantages of the methods in methylkit compare to another method ?
Thanks.

Best,
Micheal
